text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
STANDART
-- Bulgaria is expected to grant $500 per person to the country's unemployed to launch family businesses under a financial accord with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) reached last week.
-- Bulgaria's main anti-communist Union of Democratic Forces, the favourite to win the general election on April 19, launched its election campaign with a huge rally in central Sofia.
The UDF leader Ivan Kostov told the rally that a stable parliamentary majority was needed to secure the implementation of economic reforms.
-- Bulgaria is expected to receive 13 million Ecus in 1997 under the EU's PHARE programme for developing conventional energy projects, energy ministry officials said.
-- Bulgaria's State Insurance Institute, the country's biggest insurance firm, posted 1.15 billion levs pretax profit for 1996, its chairman Maxim Sirakov said.
-- Bulgaria is expected to privatise two of its six big state-owned commercial banks by end-September under a financial accord with the IMF reached last week.
PARI

-- Representatives of Russia's gas giant Gazprom are expected to visit Bulgaria for talks on gas deliveries to Bulgaria and the use of pipelines on Bulgarian terrritory within a week, the newspaper said without quoting sources.

-- Bulgaria is expected to receive the first tranche of $180 million under the funding agreement with the IMF in mid-April, interim Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski said wrapping up a visit to Washington.
KONTINENT

-- Presidential advisor Krasimir Angarski is expected to be appointed minister without portfolio in charge of implementation of Bulgaria's funding agreement with the IMF, Prime minister Stefan Sofianski said.
-- The World Bank is expected to extend $40 million loan to Bulgaria in May to support the country's balance of payments, Prime Minister Sofianski said upon return from Washington.
NOVINAR
-- Prices of Bulgaria's home-made cigarettes are expected to fall by 15 percent due to the lev rise against the dollar in March, the local cigarette maker Bulgartabac Holding said.

-- Germany is expected to invest in Bulgaria 1.5 marks annually in case the country proceeds with the implementatiin of urgent economic reforms, said the chairman of the German-Bulgarian Forum Valentin Vassilev after a visit to Germany.
-- Bulgaria's transport ministry has sold 12 transport firms since the caretaker cabinet took office in mid-February, interim Transport minister Wilhelm Kraus said.
24 CHASA
-- A trade ministry official said the ministry was planning to open privatisation procedures for 15 foreign trade firms. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
